newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL blue-chips close up on institutional buying.
newsitem.headline: KL blue-chips close up on institutional buying.

text.p: Malaysian blue-chip stocks closed sharply higher as local and foreign institutional investors moved into the Kuala Lumpur bourse, analysts and dealers said on Tuesday.

"Foreign buyers may be in today, but EPF (Employees Provident Fund) and PNB (Permodalan Nasional Bhd) have both been buying," said an institutional dealer at a local securities brokerage company. EPF is the Malaysian state-run pension fund, while PNB is a savings fund for ethnic Malays.
The Composite Index was up 9.61 points to 1189.21, while the all-share EMAS index closed up 1.51 to 339.36.

Tenaga, the day's most actively-traded blue-chip stock, was up 50 cents to 11.20 ringgit. "There is no doubt that Tenaga will be able to improve on their latest annual results," said John Engle, managing director of HG Asia in Kuala Lumpur.
"There has been a lot of interest in infrastructure-related stocks like United Engineers and Sungei Way," Engle added.
United Engineers closed up 20 cents to 20.50 ringgit, and Sungei Way was up 30 to 14.60.
Proton was up 20 cents to 16.10 ringgit on anticipation of a sharp rise in interim results due out later this month, dealers said.
